title: Petrov's Defense: the ideas
line: Black does not guard its center pawn: it attacks White's instead.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its king two squares, into the center.
Push your king pawn two squares too. It takes your share of the center.

also.c7c5: That is the Sicilian Defense, also sound. This lesson pushes the king pawn.
also.e7e6: That is the French Defense, also sound. This lesson pushes the king pawn.
also.c7c6: That is the Caro-Kann Defense, also sound. This lesson pushes the king pawn.

steps.text: Do not guard the pawn. Bring your knight out and attack White's pawn on e4 in return.

also.b8c6: Guarding the pawn with the knight is also sound and leads to other openings. This lesson attacks.
also.d7d6: That is the Philidor Defense, also sound. This lesson attacks.

steps.after: This is Petrov's Defense. White takes your pawn.

steps.text: Do not take back on e4 yet. First push the knight away with a pawn.

also.f6e4: Taking at once is also played, but it lets the white queen come out with tricks: the last lesson of this opening shows them.

steps.hint: The pawn in front of your queen can attack the knight.

steps.text: Now take the pawn on e4. The white knight has gone back, and material is level.
Push the pawn in front of your queen one more square. It guards your knight, which stands firmly in the center.

also.f8e7: That is also played. This lesson guards the knight first.

steps.after: White's bishop attacks the knight, but the pawn guards it.

steps.text: Bring the other knight out. It attacks the white pawn on d4.

also.f8e7: That is also played. This lesson brings the knight out first.
also.f8b4: That is also played. This lesson brings the knight out first.

steps.text: Bring the bishop out to clear the way for castling.
steps.after: The position is level and solid. Black gets ready to castle with nothing weak.

summary: Black answers the attack on its center pawn with an attack of its own, chases the knight first, then takes back.
